items.question: Which systems were searched to compile the filtered schedule, and was a physical file retrieved, by whom and when?
items.answer: The Museum did not identify specific systems searched or any physical file retrieval; it reiterated that no audit schedule, review log, or equivalent record of exclusion decisions exists, stating "no separate audit schedule, review log or equivalent record of exclusion decisions was created." As there is no such document, the Museum had no systems-searched detail to provide.

items.question: Does the MS 3360/3 entry name which Llandough (near Penarth or Cowbridge) 'Great House' relates to?
items.answer: Following further review, the Museum concluded the page does not relate to the farm in question at all. It said: "the page previously supplied does not relate to the property that was the subject of FOI 2026-036... it relates to a holding in the Parish of Llanfair and not to Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr, Llandough (near Penarth/Cardiff)... The document should therefore be regarded as outside the scope of FOI 2026-036."

items.question: Does Amgueddfa Cymru hold a rationale for treating certain records as outside FOI 2026-024's scope?
items.answer: No such rationale is held. The Museum said: "Amgueddfa Cymru does not hold a separate search log, file note, internal note or other recorded document setting out the rationale for that assessment." It explained that staff concluded the Church Farm and other archaeological-find records did not relate to the specific reported discovery (a soldier, horse remains and armour) and so fell outside scope, but "no separate record of that assessment was created."

items.question: Has everything found in the August 2026 searches been disclosed, or is anything withheld and under what exemption?
items.answer: The Museum confirmed "No records remain withheld," noting that the Church Farm records identified during the August searches had since been provided.

items.question: Does the MS 3360/3 page itself contain any further identifier establishing which historical Llandough is meant?
items.answer: No further identifying information was found. The Museum said: "There is no catalogue record identifying Great House Farm within this document... The information contained on that page has already been disclosed and summarised in our previous correspondence. No further recorded information relating to Great House Farm has been identified within the material held under reference MS 3360/3."

items.question: Does the MS 3360/3 page give parish, vendor, tenant or acreage detail for Great House Farm?
items.answer: Yes, to a degree. The Museum confirmed the relevant page "records that 'Great House' formed part of the Llandough Estate sale particulars of 1924, was occupied by W.G. Thomas & Sons, comprised approximately 202 acres, was situated in the Parish of Llanfair, and describes the homestead as being situated in the Village of Llandough." It stated no additional identifying information had been found within the material reviewed.

items.question: Is the Ref 13.2 waterwheel from the Penarth site opposite the hospital or the farmhouse BP demolished in 1988?
items.answer: The Museum's record describes it only as a "Waterwheel from Llandough Farm (opposite hospital)"; it confirmed "no further location information has been identified within the record," so there is nothing linking it to the farmhouse demolished by BP in 1988.

items.question: Does Amgueddfa Cymru hold a separate schedule or log of search results excluded as out of scope during its review?
items.answer: No such document is held. The Museum stated: "Amgueddfa Cymru does not hold a separate recorded document identifying, item by item, which search results were excluded following review... We do not hold a separate audit schedule of those decisions." Search results were reviewed by staff and the outcome reflected directly in the Museum's substantive response rather than in any standalone log.

items.question: Does Amgueddfa Cymru hold a schedule of records indexed as from Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr/Llandough Farm?
items.answer: Partly. The Museum said the schedules already provided under FOI 2026-032 contained the records previously identified for this location. Further enquiries for FOI 2026-036 identified two additional items: 'Ref 13.2', a waterwheel "collected from Llandough Farm" on 1 April 1979, donated by Wales and West Housing Association in connection with site development, "never formally accessioned and has subsequently been deaccessioned"; and 'MS 3360/3', a 1924 photostat copy of sale particulars for nine Vale of Glamorgan farms forming part of the Llandough Estate, within which a page relating to "Great House Farm" was identified (already provided under FOI 2026-032). The Museum stated "no further records relating specifically to Great House Farm / Ty Mawr / Llandough Farm, Llandough were identified." It later clarified, however, that neither of these two records is confirmed to relate to this particular farm: Llandough Farm is described as a separate farmstead, and the MS 3360/3 particulars may concern a different Great House Farm, near Cowbridge.

items.question: Does Amgueddfa Cymru hold 1875–1915 registers or records on Great House/Llandough Farm ironwork or finds?
items.answer: No such record was found. The Museum's response states "No 1875–1915 predecessor-register, accession, day-book, donations-book or correspondence record relating to the specified Great House / Llandough Farm ironwork or finds was identified."

items.question: Has Amgueddfa Cymru identified additional Llandough ironwork from the farmhouse floor, rear wing or dairy?
items.answer: No. The Museum confirmed that "no additional Llandough ironwork associated with the farmhouse floor, rear wing or dairy was identified."

items.question: Does Amgueddfa Cymru hold archive or accession records for Church Farm, Llandough?
items.answer: Yes. The Museum confirmed that material already retrieved for FOI 2026-024 includes archaeological accession '63.24', comprising a letter of 22 November 1931, record 63.24/1 (a rowel spur) and record 63.24/2 (a spearhead), which were supplied as attachments.

items.question: Does Amgueddfa Cymru's collections management system group catalogue records together by similar place names?
items.answer: No. The Museum stated: "our collections management system records items individually and does not group records together based on similar place names." It added that it is not aware of any recorded information showing that records for Great House Farm, Llandough (near Cowbridge) or Great House Farm, Llandow were ever catalogued or treated as relating to Great House Farm, Llandough (near Penarth/Cardiff); the similarly-named results arose from the search process, not from any overlap in the collections records themselves.

items.question: Does Amgueddfa Cymru hold reasons why certain records were judged unrelated to the 19th-century find?
items.answer: No separate recorded information is held. The Museum said: "we do not hold any separate recorded information explaining the basis on which staff concluded that the identified records were unrelated to the reported nineteenth-century discovery. That conclusion was reached through staff assessment of the available records, and no further recorded information is held."

items.question: By what date does Amgueddfa Cymru expect to respond to FOI 2026-036?
items.answer: The Museum said it aimed "to provide a response by 6th October." Its substantive response was in fact issued on 5 October 2026.

items.question: Did Amgueddfa Cymru's review find its visor/lance search used adequate terms, including military burial terms?
items.answer: The review upheld the original 'not held' decision, finding the searches reasonable and proportionate even without every suggested search term. It said: "when assessing whether information is held for the purposes of the Freedom of Information Act 2000, the relevant issue is not whether every conceivable search term has been used, but whether the authority has undertaken searches that are reasonable and proportionate in the circumstances and reasonably likely to identify relevant information if held." It confirmed the named location was used as the primary search criterion and that searches covered holdings where acquisitions, accessions, archaeological finds, provenance information and associated correspondence would reasonably be expected to be held.

items.question: What records does Amgueddfa Cymru hold on archaeological discoveries at Great House Farm and Church Farm, Llandough?
items.answer: The Museum disclosed records identified during its earlier searches, with personal data of third parties redacted. It said: "We have identified a number of records relating to archaeological discoveries recorded at Great House Farm and Church Farm, both at Llandough... Certain information has been redacted from the disclosed records under section 40(2)... where it comprises the personal data of third parties." It also pointed to publicly available material, including the 1994 Llandough early-medieval cemetery excavation report and a Cotswold Archaeology article, while noting "the provision of these records should not be taken as indicating any association."

items.question: Did Amgueddfa Cymru's internal review of FOI 2026-024 uphold the original search approach?
items.answer: Yes. The internal review upheld the original decision, finding that "the site-level search was reasonable and broader terms would be disproportionate."

items.question: What does the 'information relating generally to Great House Farm' found by Amgueddfa Cymru consist of?
items.answer: Amgueddfa Cymru did not disclose the content, stating only that the records identified fell outside the scope of the request. It said: "During the additional enquiries, a small number of records referring generally to Great House Farm, Llandough were identified. These records do not relate to furniture, furnishings, antiques, fixtures, heirlooms or other movable property originating from Great House Farm and do not fall within categories 1 to 9 of your original request. The reviewer is therefore satisfied that they fall outside the scope of the request." No further description or disclosure of these records was provided.

items.question: Did Amgueddfa Cymru search curator, donor, acquisition and disposal files for Great House Farm records?
items.answer: Amgueddfa Cymru said searches were not limited to object catalogue records and that "relevant collection documentation and associated records were also considered," but that no records were found. It stated: "No records were identified concerning furniture, furnishings, antiques, fixtures, heirlooms, or other movable property originating from Great House Farm, including correspondence with the organisations referred to in your request" (i.e. Cardiff Council, Cardiff Castle, the Bute Estate and other bodies).

items.question: Is Amgueddfa Cymru's 'no items transferred or destroyed' statement based on records or staff recollection?
items.answer: Amgueddfa Cymru said the statement reflected both the outcome of searches and staff knowledge, rather than a specific documentary record confirming transfer or destruction. It said: "The statement that the Museum is not aware of relevant records having been transferred or destroyed reflects the outcome of the searches undertaken and the knowledge of relevant collections staff. The review did not identify any records showing that information within the scope of your request had been transferred to another institution or destroyed... the Museum's position is that no relevant records were identified."

items.question: Can Amgueddfa Cymru identify which Cardiff Council/Castle archive likely holds Great House Farm furniture records?
items.answer: No. Amgueddfa Cymru said it does not hold information identifying a specific department, collection or record series at Cardiff Council or Cardiff Castle, stating: "The Museum does not hold information identifying a specific department, collection, archive or record series within Cardiff Council or Cardiff Castle that is likely to contain the information you seek." Its internal review also upheld the original 'not held' conclusion for the Museum's own records, concluding "on the balance of probabilities, the Museum does not hold recorded information falling within the scope of your request. The original decision is therefore upheld."

items.question: Which archived systems, date ranges and search terms did Amgueddfa Cymru use for Great House Farm records?
items.answer: Amgueddfa Cymru's internal review confirmed searches were undertaken but did not fully itemise individual systems, date ranges or every search term requested. It stated it was "satisfied that archived electronic records reasonably capable of containing information within scope were considered as part of the searches undertaken," and that "any data stored within a system or database pre-dating the existing Collections Management System..." (the reply text available is incomplete at this point). The review upheld the original decision that no records concerning furniture, furnishings, antiques, fixtures, heirlooms or other movable property from Great House Farm fall within categories 1-9 of the request, and confirmed the records about Great House Farm generally found during searches were treated as out of scope.

items.question: Will Amgueddfa Cymru keep FOI 2026-032 open and process it separately from FOI 2026-036?
items.answer: Yes. The Museum confirmed that "FOI:2026-032 will remain open and will be processed separately from FOI:2026-036." It explained that the earlier suggestion to merge the requests "was not made with a view to aggregating the requests or considering the application of a section 12 exemption" but was simply an administrative measure to avoid duplicated work in a small collections team; since Mr Buckler wished the requests to remain separate, the Museum agreed to proceed on that basis.

items.question: Will the internal review of FOI 2026-024 continue independently of FOI 2026-036?
items.answer: Yes. The Museum confirmed that "the internal review of FOI:2026-024 will continue independently" and that nothing in FOI 2026-036 should be read as commenting on that review.

items.question: Did Amgueddfa Cymru's internal review of FOI 2026-020 (furniture and household contents) uphold the original decision?
items.answer: Yes. The internal review of FOI 2026-020, concerning furniture and household contents, was upheld.

items.question: Does Amgueddfa Cymru hold a visor and lance said found beneath Great House Farm's dining-room floor?
items.answer: No. Amgueddfa Cymru said: "We have not identified any records relating to the acquisition, accession, donation, transfer or deposit of a medieval visor, lance, helmet or other item of armour associated with Great House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough. We have also not identified records relating to the specific discovery described in your request, including records of associated human or animal remains, reburial records, excavation reports, watching briefs or discovery reports." It added that, for completeness, its searches had identified records relating to other archaeological finds at Church Farm, Llandough, and other archaeological discoveries at Great House Farm, but considered these unrelated to the discovery described in the request and outside its scope.

items.question: What searches did Amgueddfa Cymru carry out to conclude it holds no Great House Farm furniture records?
items.answer: Amgueddfa Cymru set out the searches undertaken. It said it reviewed records across the Museum's collections and had its IT team review "archived electronic systems and records." For the History collections, it searched "the Collections Management System (CMS), accession files, donor indexes, location indexes and associated collection documentation" using the terms "Great House Farm", "Ty Mawr", "Llandough", "Buckler" and "Bute". For the Art collections, it searched description, comments, acquisition notes and place fields using "Ty Mawr", "Great House Farm", "Great House", "Williams", "Buckler", "Llandough" and combinations of those terms; no additional paper archives were identified. These enquiries identified "some information relating generally to Great House Farm and the surrounding area" but nothing concerning furniture or household objects, and the Museum said it was "not aware of any relevant collection records relating to such material having been transferred to another institution or destroyed."

items.question: Does Amgueddfa Cymru hold furniture, furnishings, fixtures or heirlooms from Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough?
items.answer: No. Amgueddfa Cymru replied that, following searches of its collections management systems and associated records, it had "not identified any furniture, furnishings, antiques, fixtures, heirlooms or other movable property recorded as originating from Great House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough." It stated it had found no inventories, catalogues, acquisition records, disposal records, loan records, provenance files, ownership records, photographs, correspondence, reports or memoranda falling within the scope of the request. It noted that archaeological finds from the land were outside the scope of this particular request and were being dealt with as a separate information request. The Museum's formal position was: "Under section 1(1)(a) of the Freedom of Information Act 2000, our response is therefore that Amgueddfa Cymru does not hold the requested information."

items.question: To which repositories were surviving pre-1997 Welsh Office/Welsh Government records transferred?
items.answer: Welsh Government replied that historical material would normally have been transferred to The National Archives or another designated Place of Deposit, stating: "Historical material would then have been transferred by us to The National Archives (or a designated Place of Deposit)". It did not identify a specific transfer record for any Great House Farm material.

items.question: Were Cadw/Welsh Office files on Great House Farm transferred, destroyed or disposed, under what schedule?
items.answer: Cadw refused to answer this part of the request, treating it as repeated. Its substantive reply of 19 October 2026 refused the request under FOIA section 14(2) as "substantially similar" to the earlier ATISN 27021 request, stating "no new information has been generated or become available since our previous response," and referred the requester to the published ATISN 27021 release and review rather than giving details of any transfer, destruction or disposal.

items.question: Do retention schedules show if files mentioning Great House Farm, Western Ground Rents or BP were destroyed?
items.answer: The Welsh Government's Operational Effectiveness Group, replying for the Departmental Records Officer, said its searches found no files mentioning the farm, Western Ground Rents Ltd or BP Properties Ltd, and that "any routine records would have been destroyed in line with the corporate retention schedule applied at the time", or disposal may have been carried out by a predecessor body. It explained that before 1997 the Welsh Office and other agencies had their own retention schedules, that historical material would have been selected under The National Archives' Operational Selection Policy OSP 7 (Welsh Office 1979–1997), and that property, deeds and lease records are "not classed as 'public records'" and are kept until the property is sold or the lease ends. An internal review was offered within 40 working days (by 14 December 2026). The reply states that this negative search result, dated 19 October 2026, "does not establish that records never existed."

items.question: Does Cadw hold an inventory of the 1988 listing file for Great House Farm?
items.answer: This request is pending. Cadw registered the request as ATISN 26-0009, due 6 November 2026; no substantive reply has yet been received.

items.question: Does PEDW hold records on Great House Farm or applications 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES?
items.answer: No, PEDW replied that it holds no such records. Its Head of Operations said: "Planning and Environment Decisions Wales (PEDW) does not hold any information or records for Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth or planning applications 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES. All PEDW's electronic records have been searched. PEDW does not have a paper file repository."

items.question: Has Cadw's 2017 guidance on Historic Environment Records been reviewed since 2023 Act sections 194-196?
items.answer: No substantive answer has yet been given. The Welsh Government's ministerial correspondence unit acknowledged the enquiry (ref TO/HF/05677/26) on 30 September 2026 and said a response was due within 17 working days, by 23 October 2026; it did not address whether the 2017 guidance has been substantively reviewed.

items.question: When was current statutory guidance under section 196 of the 2023 Act issued and laid before Senedd?
items.answer: No substantive answer has yet been given. The Welsh Government's ministerial correspondence unit only acknowledged the enquiry (ref TO/HF/05677/26) on 30 September 2026, saying a response was due by 23 October 2026.

items.question: Does current section 196 guidance address record classification and the public interface behaviour?
items.answer: No substantive answer has yet been given. The Welsh Government's ministerial correspondence unit only acknowledged the enquiry (ref TO/HF/05677/26) on 30 September 2026, saying a response was due by 23 October 2026.

items.question: Did Welsh Government acknowledge the preservation notice covering Great House Farm records sent on 28 September 2026?
items.answer: No reply has been received. A preservation notice was sent to Welsh Government officials on 28 September 2026 and repeated on 1 October 2026, asking the department to "preserve, and do not destroy, transfer out of your custody without a written receipt, or dispose of, any file, plan, photograph, tape or electronic record" relating to Great House Farm. Welsh Government has not confirmed receipt or compliance with the notice.

items.question: Was the 1982 GGAT information available to Cadw before its 1988 listing decision on Great House Farm?
items.answer: No substantive answer has yet been given. The only reply received acknowledged the complaint and said it had been passed on for consideration: Cadw's email said, "We have forwarded your complaint to our complaints manager." No findings on the 1982 GGAT information have been provided.

items.question: Does Cadw hold evidence of what archaeological or planning information was available in 1988?
items.answer: No substantive answer has yet been given. The only reply received acknowledged the complaint and said it had been forwarded to Cadw's complaints manager, without addressing whether any such evidence survives.

items.question: Did Cadw discuss with planning/archaeological authorities the need to protect Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr)?
items.answer: No substantive answer has yet been given. Cadw's reply only acknowledged the complaint and said it had been forwarded to its complaints manager.

items.question: Did Cadw discuss temporary protection to prevent Great House Farm's demolition pending 1988 listing?
items.answer: No substantive answer has yet been given. Cadw's reply only acknowledged the complaint and said it had been forwarded to its complaints manager; the question about temporary protection discussions (e.g. a Building Preservation Notice) was not addressed.

items.question: Did Cadw provide any further explanation of its 1988 listing decision and the loss of the related file?
items.answer: No further explanation was given. Cadw's final reply stated "There is nothing further that I can add … it would be inappropriate for me to speculate … this final reply", closing the correspondence and directing any further contact to the Welsh Government complaints process or to Freedom.ofinformation@gov.wales rather than to the individual official.

items.question: Can Cadw add anything further on the 1988 listing assessment of Great House Farm given the lack of contemporary records?
items.answer: No, Cadw's Chief Inspector said all held records had already been provided and nothing further could be added. Dr Andy Wigley, Chief Inspector - Head of Historic Environment Inspectorate, stated: 'we have now provided all the information that we hold... There is nothing further that I can add to our previous replies, and it would be inappropriate for me to speculate on the events around the listing assessment without our own contemporary evidence being available to me to substantiate precisely what occurred.' He signposted the Welsh Government complaints process for further dissatisfaction.

items.question: What pre-1988 architectural/archaeological evidence on Great House Farm did the 1988 inspector consider?
items.answer: No reply has been received to this question, sent 28 August 2026.

items.question: What was Cadw's historic and current record retention policy for files relating to unsuccessful listing decisions?
items.answer: Cadw said it cannot state the exact 1988 retention arrangements but current staff believe unsuccessful listing files were historically kept only briefly. Cadw explained: 'it is not possible to say exactly what CADW's retention arrangements were over 38 years ago. However, based on their knowledge of the systems in place at the time, current colleagues have advised that it is likely that records of unsuccessful listings were only retained for a short period, usually about 3 years. This has since changed and current retention policy in relation to unsuccessful listings is to retain the files indefinitely, reviewed every 5 years.'

items.question: Did Cadw's 1988 assessment of Great House Farm take into account the H.J. Thomas RCAHMW survey of 1974?
items.answer: Cadw said it cannot determine this from the surviving records. It replied: 'As stated, all of the records we hold have been released to you under the FOI and are now a public record. As the release consists of only two photographs we are unable to determine whether or not the 1974 survey was taken into account at the time.'

items.question: Who manages the Historic Environment Record content for Great House Farm and how can new information be added?
items.answer: Cadw said the HER is managed by a third party, not Cadw itself. It replied: 'content of the HER is managed by Heneb. Please contact www.heneb.org.uk in relation to adding information to the HER.'

items.question: Where 1988 assessment records no longer survive, will Cadw acknowledge this evidential limitation?
items.answer: No reply has been received to this question, sent 28 August 2026.

items.question: Does Cadw hold transfer lists, accession records or archive schedules showing Great House Farm records sent to RCAHMW?
items.answer: No. Cadw stated: 'We have no record of any transfer lists, accession records, archive schedules or other documentation recording whether records relating to Great House Farm were ever transferred to the RCAHMW.' Cadw added that an inspector had advised, based on personal experience rather than any surviving document, that the practice at the time was to either transfer such records to the RCAHMW or destroy them under the Public Records Act 1958.

items.question: What is the only surviving documentary evidence that Cadw visited and assessed Great House Farm in 1988?
items.answer: Cadw said the only surviving documentary evidence is the photograph from the site visit. It stated: 'The photograph provides the only documentary evidence that Great House Farm was visited by Cadw and did not meet the criteria as it was not included on the list.' Cadw confirmed it holds no further information to assist the search.

items.question: Besides the two 1988 photos, does any inspection report or case file on Great House Farm survive?
items.answer: No reply has been received to this question, raised on 29 July 2026.

items.question: What is the documentary basis for Cadw's conclusion that Great House Farm did not meet the listing criteria?
items.answer: Cadw said the conclusion rests on two surviving photographs of the property dated 29 July 1988. Cadw explained that 'the two photographs illustrate that the building was inspected for listing and 'yyy' reference on the reverse of the photograph was the coding at the time to signify that the building did not met the criteria to be listed.'

items.question: Does Cadw hold an official listing file for Great House Farm beyond the two 1988 photographs?
items.answer: No, Cadw said no such file has been located. It explained that 'the practice was to keep all photographs separate from the official file in a cabinet. No official file containing additional information has been located and the Records Department have indicated that the documentation from 1988 has, most likely, been destroyed.'

items.question: What is the evidential basis for Cadw's statement that the 1988 Great House Farm records may have been destroyed?
items.answer: Cadw said there is no formal destruction record; the statement was based on internal professional judgement rather than documentary evidence. It stated: 'No destruction record exists. An official in the Records Department provided this advice based on their experience and understanding of the records within their management.'

items.question: Did Cadw's searches for records relating to Great House Farm cover all relevant record categories?
items.answer: Yes. Cadw confirmed: 'I can confirm that the searches included all 8 categories.'

items.question: Was Great House Farm actually considered for statutory listing in 1988?
items.answer: Yes, Cadw confirmed the building was considered for listing, though almost all records of that consideration are now lost. Cadw stated: 'I can confirm that the building was considered for listing, however other than the 2 photographs provided, no other records survive.' This answered the alternative put to Cadw as to whether the property was never considered, was considered but records are lost, or whether it is now impossible to tell.

items.question: Does Cadw hold any records from the 1970s to 1990s relating to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr?
items.answer: No. Cadw's response to ATISN 27021 states: “Following a search of our paper and electronic records, apart from the two photographs, I have established that the information you require is not held by the Welsh Government. Any other associated records would have been either transferred to the Royal Commission … for permanent preservation, or destroyed under the Public Record Act 1958.”

items.question: Does Cadw hold any photographs, plans, surveys or architectural records relating to Great House Farm?
items.answer: Cadw acknowledged this request (part of ATISN 27021) on 1 June 2026, stating a response would be sent by 25 June 2026. Cadw's substantive reply, received 11 June 2026, said "Please see attached response and documents"; the specific content of those attached documents is not reproduced in the correspondence available here.

items.question: Does Cadw hold correspondence on the historic significance or preservation of Great House Farm?
items.answer: Cadw acknowledged this request (part of ATISN 27021) on 1 June 2026, with a due date of 25 June 2026. Cadw's reply of 11 June 2026 states "Please see attached response and documents"; the specific content of those documents is not reproduced in the correspondence available here.

items.question: Does Cadw hold records explaining why Great House Farm was not added to the statutory list of special buildings?
items.answer: Cadw acknowledged this request (part of ATISN 27021) on 1 June 2026, with a due date of 25 June 2026. Cadw's reply of 11 June 2026 states "Please see attached response and documents"; the specific content of those documents is not reproduced in the correspondence available here.

items.question: Does Cadw hold records on the age, architectural or archaeological significance of Great House Farm?
items.answer: Cadw acknowledged this request (part of ATISN 27021) on 1 June 2026, with a due date of 25 June 2026. Cadw's reply of 11 June 2026 states "Please see attached response and documents"; the specific content of those documents is not reproduced in the correspondence available here.

items.question: Does Cadw hold records on emergency listing or preservation measures considered for Great House Farm?
items.answer: Cadw acknowledged this request (part of ATISN 27021) on 1 June 2026, with a due date of 25 June 2026. Cadw's reply of 11 June 2026 states "Please see attached response and documents"; the specific content of those documents is not reproduced in the correspondence available here.

items.question: Does Cadw hold records of public campaigns, petitions or representations seeking preservation of Great House Farm?
items.answer: Cadw acknowledged this request (part of ATISN 27021) on 1 June 2026, with a due date of 25 June 2026. Cadw's reply of 11 June 2026 states "Please see attached response and documents"; the specific content of those documents is not reproduced in the correspondence available here.

items.question: Does Welsh Government hold archaeological assessments, surveys or heritage impact reports for Great House Farm?
items.answer: No reply has been received. The request, sent 7 June 2026, asked for any archaeological assessments, surveys, reports, briefs, watching briefs, excavation reports, or heritage impact assessments relating to the site.

items.question: Did Cadw's 1988 Llandough survey assess Great House Farm and its barn for listing, and were they rejected?
items.answer: Yes. Cadw's reply of 21 May 2026 confirmed that Great House Farm and its barn were assessed during the 1988 community survey of Llandough and were rejected for listing. Two photographs dated 29 July 1988 were enclosed, marked “YYY”, which Cadw explained means “marginally below the bar”.

items.question: Does the single paper file found by Cadw, dated 2002, mention Great House Farm?
items.answer: No. Cadw's reply of 21 May 2026 stated that the one paper file it had located, dated 2002, does not mention the farm.

items.question: Did Cadw ever complete a formal heritage review of the demolition of Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr)?
items.answer: Cadw's Listed Buildings team confirmed a 1988 listing assessment but found no record of a formal review of the demolition itself, and further searches were still underway. The reply stated: 'I have searched our electronic records relating to Great House Farm and Barn and I can confirm they were assessed and rejected for listing in the 1988 community survey of Llandough,' attaching two photographs dated 29 July 1988 whose 'YYY' marking indicated the buildings were 'considered marginally below the bar for listing.' Cadw said 'We hold no other electronic records.' It noted a South Wales Echo report suggesting Cadw inspectors would revisit the site in December 1988, but added 'I can find no record (as-yet) of this.' A single paper file dated 2002 was located but 'makes no mention of Great House Farm.' Cadw said it had asked a colleague to search for other paper files, including Welsh Office files, warning that 'it is quite likely that at least some of these files will have been destroyed,' but undertook to disclose any further records recovered.

items.question: Will Cadw consider a renewed historical or heritage examination of Great House Farm's demolition?
items.answer: Cadw did not commit to a renewed examination in its reply, but said it would continue searching for further paper records (including Welsh Office files) and would write again once that search was complete, which it estimated 'may take a couple of weeks.' In the meantime, Cadw signposted other archives that might hold relevant material, including Glamorgan Archives, the National Library of Wales, and the Royal Commission on the Ancient & Historical Monuments of Wales (Coflein).

items.question: Does Cadw's Cof Cymru database list Great House Farm, Llandough as a designated historic asset?
items.answer: Cadw replied that no designated historic assets relevant to Great House Farm appear on the Cof Cymru database: 'Upon reviewing the Cof Cymru database, I found that there are no designated historic assets relevant to this topic.' However, Cadw noted that the Archwilio Historic Environment Record contains two relevant entries documenting the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust's (GGAT) involvement: the 'Great House Farm HER site entry' (GGAT03586s) and the 'Land at Great House Farm HER event entry' (GGATE003872), the latter including GGAT's 1990 archaeological assessment report commissioned by BP Properties Ltd. Cadw suggested contacting the Royal Commission's National Monuments Record of Wales (NMRW), Heneb, and the Vale of Glamorgan Local Planning Authority for any further records.

items.question: Does Cadw hold records of a Roman soldier reportedly discovered beneath Great House Farm in 1888?
items.answer: Cadw indicated it holds no record of this discovery and that any such find would not have been formally registered at the time. Cadw's Historic Environment Inspectorate replied that 'any such find would typically have been reported in the antiquarian press at either the national or local level' and that records of this kind might instead be held by local museums. It added that the first Ancient Monuments Act (1882) dealt only with monuments brought into guardianship, and that 'the legal recognition of nationally important archaeology did not come about until the Ancient Monuments Consolidation and Amendment Act of 1913' — meaning no statutory mechanism existed in 1888 to record or protect such a find.

items.question: Does Cadw hold records of archaeological notifications or 1990s excavation finds at Great House Farm?
items.answer: No reply has been received to this part of the request. Sion Buckler asked Cadw for 'records of any archaeological notifications, alerts, or discoveries associated with Great House Farm, whether before or after demolition, including references to artefacts later recovered during excavations in the early 1990s'. The request was sent on 23 January 2026 and no response is recorded in the correspondence.

items.question: Does Cadw hold records linking Great House Farm to early radio experimentation, including Marconi?
items.answer: No reply has been received to this part of the request. Sion Buckler asked Cadw for 'any documentation referring to historical associations between Great House Farm and early radio or wireless experimentation, including any mention of Guglielmo Marconi or related activity in the Cardiff Bay / Lavernock / surrounding area that may have been considered or dismissed'. The request was sent on 23 January 2026 and no response is recorded.

items.question: Has CPS reviewed the Great House Farm evidence bundle submitted 30 Sept 2026, and what advice given?
items.answer: No substantive reply has yet been received. The CPS's Victim Liaison Unit acknowledged the 30 September correspondence, apologising for the delay, and said "Your email has been passed to a CPS manager for her advice, and we will return to you when we receive that advice." No further response is recorded.

items.question: Does CPS hold a file on Sion Buckler's Great House Farm reports, or should he report elsewhere?
items.answer: The CPS replied that it could not locate a case file from the information provided. The Victim Liaison Officer wrote: "Unfortunately, I have been unable to locate a case file based on the information provided. Our reference numbers are known as Unique Reference Numbers (URNs) and follow a format similar to: 62HA... followed by seven digits." The CPS asked Mr Buckler to contact the officer in the case to request a CPS reference number if one had been issued, and to provide the necessary information by 13 October 2026.

items.question: Would the CPS take over a private prosecution under s.6(2) POA 1985 re Great House Farm?
items.answer: The CPS said it could not give an advance opinion on this hypothetical. Its Victim Liaison Unit replied that it is "unable to provide an opinion on that issue in advance" and that "any decision as to whether the CPS would take over a private prosecution can only be made after considering the specific facts, evidence and circumstances of the individual case". It added that it was "not in a position to say whether the CPS would or would not take over any future private prosecution".

items.question: Should Great House Farm be referred to an investigative authority before CPS takes over proceedings?
items.answer: Yes, the CPS advised reporting to the police first. It stated "If you believe that a criminal offence has been committed, you should report the matter to the police" and that "It is the responsibility of the police to investigate any allegation and determine whether there is sufficient evidence to refer the case to the Crown Prosecution Service for a charging decision."

items.question: Which CPS division or office should the Great House Farm evidential bundle be submitted to?
items.answer: No reply addressing this specific question has been received. The CPS's substantive response of 9 September 2026 dealt only with the hypothetical private-prosecution and referral questions and did not identify a division or office for submission of the evidential bundle.

items.question: Does DCMS hold information on furniture, furnishings, heirlooms or other movable property from Great House Farm?
items.answer: DCMS replied that it holds no information on this subject. The FOI response dated 22 July 2026 stated that no information was held relating to furniture, furnishings, heirlooms or other movable property from Great House Farm. The family questioned this, saying they were surprised no information was held, and requested an internal review. DCMS's internal review, completed on 19 August 2026, upheld the original nil response.

items.question: Does D153/1-8 contain any 1875-1880 item naming Thomas Williams, Daniel Thomas or the dwelling by St Dochdwy's?
items.answer: Glamorgan Archives did not hold or search this material itself and redirected the enquiry. It replied that "the majority of your email relates to document reference D153/1–8... this is a reference for material held at the National Library of Wales so you should contact them about these records," pointing to the Library's online catalogue entry describing "Deeds relating to premises in p. Llandough, co. Glam., comprising a dwelling house adjoining the churchyard, 1811 (D153/1-2), land...".

items.question: What does reference DRA/11/120 (formerly D/DRa 11/120) relate to, and does it connect to Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr?
items.answer: Glamorgan Archives said it is not connected to Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr. It replied that "D/DRa 11/120 is an old way of formatting our reference DRA/11/120," forming part of series DRA/11/1-293, which "comprises lawsuits, instructions to counsel, opinions etc. relating to undermining of house property, flooding, contravention of colliery regulations, 1856-1909 in respect of Elder's Navigation Colliery, Maesteg," adding "this doesn't seem relevant to your research and doesn't relate to Tynywain either" and asking the requester to clarify the reference's source.

items.question: Does Glamorgan Archives hold any record of the 1877 Daniel Thomas–Bute Estate transaction at Llandough?
items.answer: No such record is held. Glamorgan Archives said: “we do not appear to hold any deeds relating to this transaction. A search of our catalogue has been carried out and we cannot suggest any documents that would be worth searching to find record of the transaction you are seeking information on that are within our collections.” It noted a possible lead in Cardiff Library's (not-yet-transferred) Bute Estate records: reference Bute X.6(12), “which contains abstracts of payments and receipts by the trustees of the Marquis of Bute's properties, 1877 (copy),” and suggested other items in the Bute X series might also be relevant, advising direct contact with Cardiff Library.

items.question: Will Glamorgan Archives search the D696 Western Ground Rents volumes for references to Llandough or Great House Farm?
items.answer: Glamorgan Archives had not carried out the search itself at the time of reply but offered to do so for a charge, or said the volumes could be consulted free of charge in the searchroom. It stated: “Only once the records have been searched would we be able to confirm whether any information is held within them in relation to land in Llandough and Ty Mawr / Great House Farm.” Catalogue descriptions of the three volumes (D696/1, D696/2, D696/3) were provided.

items.question: Which Ordnance Survey sheet corresponds to the 1910 Land Valuation Survey map for the Llandough area?
items.answer: Glamorgan Archives advised that the relevant Ordnance Survey sheet is Glamorgan XLVII.6, and referred the requester to The National Archives' research guide on the 1910–1915 Valuation Office Survey for how to obtain the corresponding maps, since Glamorgan Archives does not hold them.

items.question: Does the 1939 Western Ground Rents tenancy plan match the requester's described land parcel arrangement?
items.answer: No reply has been received to this question.

items.question: Do the Thomas/Williams/quarrying records show the farmhouse parcel treated differently by 1928?
items.answer: No reply has been received to this question.

items.question: Does the 1938 Western Ground Rents conveyance show acquisition of the farmhouse plot or just agricultural land?
items.answer: No reply has been received to this question.

items.question: Does the 1939 Western Ground Rents tenancy plan cover only the eastern parcel, excluding the farmhouse?
items.answer: No reply has been received to this question.

items.question: Do records show any 1955, 1962 or 1974 act transferring or extinguishing the family's farmhouse interest?
items.answer: No reply has been received to this question.

items.question: Do Glamorgan Archives' records show how the farmhouse parcel passed to Western Ground Rents or BP by 1982/83?
items.answer: No reply has been received to this question.

items.question: Is the Nov 1877 Llandough counterpart lease the same as DBDT/18/1, with a July 1877 copy under DBDT/1/3?
items.answer: Glamorgan Archives confirmed two separate items. It replied: "I think the items described below have been discussed previously – are these what you are seeking?" and listed DBDT/1/3, described as "Adamsdown Square leases from the trustees of the will of the late Marquess of Bute. Lease to Mr John Williams", dated July 1877, and DBDT/18/1, described as "Lease (counterpart) of land and premises situate in Clyde Street, Roath from the trustees of the Will of the late Marquess of Bute to Mr John Williams", dated Nov 1877 — the item already photographed. The archive asked the requester to confirm these were the items sought before quoting for copies.

items.question: Does Glamorgan Archives' digital photography order form and pricing apply to a customer based overseas (Patagonia)?
items.answer: Yes. Glamorgan Archives replied that the attached digital photography order form "applies wherever you are based" and noted that "prices quoted do not include VAT due to your location", asking the requester to sign and agree to the declaration on the order form.

items.question: Does Glamorgan Archives hold any record explaining why the fabric of Great House Farm was not scheduled before 1988?
items.answer: No. Glamorgan Archives replied that this is “Not held in our collections” and suggested contacting Cadw and the Royal Commission on the Ancient and Historical Monuments of Wales instead.

items.question: Does Glamorgan Archives hold records of when Great House Farm archaeology was raised in planning?
items.answer: Glamorgan Archives did not confirm whether such a record exists, stating only: “If any record of this is in our collections it would appear in the Planning Committee records described above in point 6,” without confirming a specific record had been found.

items.question: Does the DXJF/64/27-32 sketch bundle include a sketch of the former layout of Llandough-juxta-Penarth village?
items.answer: Yes. Glamorgan Archives identified the relevant items as DXJF/64/30-31: “sketch of former layout of part of village of Llandough-juxta-Penarth by Mrs. Nancy Buckler of great house farm, Llandough, with notes c1950 [1 card, 1 paper].” It asked the requester to confirm whether this matched material already seen, noting the other items in the bundle do not relate to Llandough.

items.question: After examining DBDT/79/1, did Glamorgan Archives confirm whether it differs from the Nov 1877 Llandough counterpart?
items.answer: Glamorgan Archives stated "These points were answered in my email of 14th September." That reply covered the examination and photography of DBDT/79/1 (catalogued May 1877, Pembroke Terrace) and included a digital photography order form.

items.question: Is DBDT79/1 a lease dated 2 May 1877 between the Marquess of Bute's trustees and Mr John Williams?
items.answer: Yes. Glamorgan Archives confirmed: “The document is a counterpart lease dated 2 May 1877 between the Trustees of the Will of the late Marquess of Bute and Mr John Williams of Newport.”

items.question: What is the exact property description in deed DBDT79/1, and does it locate the property in Pembroke Terrace, Cardiff?
items.answer: Yes, the deed locates the property in Pembroke Terrace. Glamorgan Archives quoted the description in full: “All that piece or parcel of land with the messuage or tenement and outbuildings thereto now being erected and built or part thereof by the said lesee, situate, lying and being in Pembroke Terrace in the parish of St John the Baptist, Cardiff containing by admeasurement sixty-nine feet or thereabouts on the north side thereof, thirty-one feet or thereabouts on the east and west sides thereof and sixty-nine feet six inches or thereabouts on the south side thereof bounded on the north by land of the Marquess of Bute, on the east by Pembroke Terrace aforesaid, on the south by land demised to David Price and on the west by land of Mr John William Vachell.”

items.question: Does deed DBDT79/1 mention Llandough, Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr, Western Ground Rents, or other localities?
items.answer: No. Glamorgan Archives confirmed: “There is no mention of Llandough, Great House Farm or Ty Mawr or any other property outside of Pembroke Terrace.”

items.question: Does the marginal plan on DBDT79/1 clearly identify the property's location?
items.answer: Yes. Glamorgan Archives said: “The plan clearly shows a property on Pembroke Terrace.” A digital copy could be supplied for a charge of £15.60 (inclusive of VAT).

items.question: Does DBDT79/1 include further details like adjoining owners, plot numbers, rent or cross-references?
items.answer: No. Glamorgan Archives stated: “There is no further information included,” beyond the description already quoted from the deed.

items.question: Was the DBDT79/1 catalogue description, which named only 'the Marquess of Bute' rather than his trustees, correct?
items.answer: No; Glamorgan Archives confirmed the catalogue description for DBDT/79/1 'had a few small errors which have now been corrected' and that the document is a counterpart lease dated 2 May 1877 between the Trustees of the Will of the late Marquess of Bute and Mr John Williams of Newport.

items.question: Did Glamorgan Archives identify Daniel Thomas in DBDT/10/19-20 and address the Bute-Thomas search and costs?
items.answer: Glamorgan Archives stated "These points were answered in my email of 7th September." That 7 September reply gave answers on DBDT/10/19 and the related Bute, Mountjoy and D696 holdings, and enclosed 41 Bute catalogue documents as a ZIP file.

items.question: How much would it cost to obtain a digital copy of document reference ACA/8/2 from Glamorgan Archives?
items.answer: Glamorgan Archives quoted £60 for the full copy. It replied that the volume "contains 106 pages so would require 53 images – total cost £60 (for one hour work)", under its standard charges of £15.60 for a single image and £4.80 for each subsequent image from the same document, or £60 per hour for multiple images from multiple documents. The requester was asked to complete and return the attached form to proceed.

items.question: Does Glamorgan Archives list any deeds, besides DBDT10/19 and DBDT10/20, linking the Thomases to the Bute Estate?
items.answer: No further deeds were found. Glamorgan Archives replied: “There are no additional deeds described on our catalogue between Daniel or Alfred Thomas and the Bute Estate.”

items.question: Does Glamorgan Archives hold Daniel Thomas's will linking him to the Llandough lime works or Great House Farm?
items.answer: Glamorgan Archives did not supply or confirm holding such a will. It advised that if the requester did not already have a copy of Daniel Thomas's will, they could apply for a copy of probate from the Probate Office, pointing to the gov.uk guidance 'Search probate records for documents and wills (England and Wales)'.

items.question: Did the Bute Estate later reacquire any parcel of land previously linked to Daniel Thomas?
items.answer: Glamorgan Archives could not confirm this directly, stating: “We do not hold the majority of the Bute Estate records.” It supplied a finding aid to the Bute Estate records held by Cardiff Library (which were due to transfer to Glamorgan Archives) and noted that other Bute Estate records are held at the National Library of Wales.

items.question: Did Mountjoy Ltd or Western Ground Rents Ltd acquire title to land previously held by Daniel Thomas or his successors?
items.answer: Glamorgan Archives did not confirm this directly but pointed to collection D696, noting it “includes a book plans and rental books for land owned by Western Ground Rents Ltd c1938-1944,” without confirming whether the land in question is actually documented in it.

items.question: What identifying details does deed DBDT10/19 give for Daniel Thomas?
items.answer: Glamorgan Archives confirmed that DBDT/10/19 describes Daniel Thomas as “of the Town of Cardiff, Builder” and that “There are no further identifying details for Daniel Thomas in the documents.” Digital copies could be supplied for a charge, or the documents viewed free of charge in the public searchroom.

items.question: Does Glamorgan Archives hold estate maps or valuation plans showing boundaries of Great House Farm?
items.answer: Glamorgan Archives said it does not hold the corresponding maps for the 1910 Land Valuation book covering Llandough. It stated that a staff member “consulted the 1910 Land Valuation book for Llandough (DVAL/1/33) but we do not have the corresponding maps to go with this – you would need to contact the National Archives for a copy of this.” It also suggested checking historic Ordnance Survey plans, for example via the National Library of Scotland's online Map Finder.

items.question: Has HM Land Registry opened an internal application to investigate the error affecting title WA231076?
items.answer: Yes. HM Land Registry confirmed that the matter had already been raised and that an application had been captured internally for investigation and correction. The reply states: “The matter you have contacted us about has already been raised by yourself and an application has been captured internally by HM Land Registry to investigate and correct any error that may have been made.” The new internal application reference given was Z084NQV.

items.question: Can HM Land Registry provide a copy of the register for the closed title WA240304?
items.answer: No copy is available because the title no longer exists on the register. HM Land Registry's reply states: “I have looked at the title number you have quoted and this is not a current title number, this title appears to have been closed in 2005 and therefore no copy of the register is available.” The reply suggested using the department's property search service for the address instead.

items.question: Does 'not aware of any question or doubt affecting title' appear in Form 1E (WA231076 item 13) or elsewhere?
items.answer: No substantive answer has been received. HM Land Registry's reply was an automated message stating that “the wrong contact information was shown on our letter to you” and directing the enquirer to the online contact form, without confirming where (or whether) the certificate wording survives.

items.question: Is the marriage certificate Mr Gill relied on held on the WA231076 file, the 30 July 2026 schedule, or not held?

items.question: Do the 30 July 2026 WA231076/WA240304 records mention Williams, Buckler, Great House Farm, or title disputes?

items.answer: No substantive answer has been received. items.question: What do Form D23 and the 8 April 1983 letter from Linklaters & Paines (WA240304 item 7) concern?
items.answer: No substantive answer has been received. items.question: Does the 1971 Abstract of Title connected with title WA231076 still survive, and where is it held?
items.answer: No substantive answer has been received. The only reply was an automated message stating: “I am sorry that the wrong contact information was shown on our letter to you. items.question: Which item numbers should be requested via Form OC2 for fullest first-registration records, title WA231076?
items.answer: No substantive answer has been received. HM Land Registry's reply was an automated message explaining a contact-details error and asking the enquirer to use its online contact form, without identifying specific item numbers for an OC2 application.

items.answer: HM Land Registry supplied a letter listing the surviving first-registration documents for the title. The 30 July letter enclosed a schedule of 43 such documents, which is catalogued separately (GHF-E106-10).

items.answer: No. HM Land Registry's Information Rights team said it could not answer general registration enquiries and referred the matter to Customer Support and to the statutory routes of access for register information, rather than dealing with it under FOI.

items.question: If a marriage certificate formed part of Great House Farm's registration evidence, can copies of it be requested?
items.answer: No reply has been received. Sion Buckler asked HM Land Registry to identify any document relied upon as evidence of identity continuity and whether copies could be requested, but no response is recorded in the correspondence.

items.question: Does HM Land Registry hold recorded information under FOIA about land on the north side of Leckwith Road, Llandough?
items.answer: HM Land Registry confirmed it holds recorded information about this land, but said it is contained in registers open to public inspection and is therefore available through the statutory routes of access under the Land Registration Act 2002 (ss.66–67) rather than under FOIA.

items.question: Does HM Land Registry hold records from 1938–1987 relating to Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough, near Penarth?
items.answer: HM Land Registry did not provide the requested historic records and indicated the request would likely be refused. It first replied that it needed the title number before it could proceed, stating: “To assist you in accessing information held by HMLR, please be aware the information you have requested is held within our registers that are open to public inspection and accessible via statutory routes of access. This means that we are unable to provide access to this information via an Environmental Information Regulations (EIR) or a Freedom of Information Act 2000 (FOIA) request and it is likely a refusal notice will be issued for this information.” After Mr Buckler supplied a letter intended to identify the plot, HM Land Registry said: “the information you have provided does not assist us in locating the title number. We are unable to proceed with your Freedom of Information request without this information,” and directed him to its Customer Support team instead. A further message on 13 April 2026 said a formal response to the FOI request was attached, but the content of that attachment is not recorded in the correspondence supplied.

items.question: Will HM Land Registry review the 1982 Great House Farm application files for undisclosed ownership interests?
items.answer: HM Land Registry has not yet given a substantive answer; the matter has been passed to a senior officer for review. Haste wrote: "The information provided has been noted and referred to a senior officer. Due to the complexity of the issues raised please allow enough time for the senior officer to review and investigate your comments and reply to you accordingly." No further reply is recorded in the correspondence.

items.question: Did HM Land Registry reply to Stephen Doughty MP's enquiry about Great House Farm?
items.answer: Yes, HM Land Registry's Chief Executive and Chief Land Registrar sent a reply directly to Stephen Doughty MP's office in September 2026 (reference 260900). The content of that reply has not been supplied in this bundle, so it cannot be quoted here. The MP's office said it was still awaiting a response from the Ministry of Justice on the related matter.

items.question: Does Heneb hold the Trust's response to application 92/00671/RES or correspondence with Wyn Thomas or Ideal Homes?
items.answer: Heneb (as the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust's Historic Environment Record) replied that “the HER does not hold information relating to this request.” The reply was scoped specifically to the HER rather than to the Trust's wider records as originally asked, so it is not yet clear whether a search was made of non-HER Trust files.

items.question: Does Heneb hold records of its 1993 notification to the Vale of Glamorgan that groundworks breached Condition 18?
items.answer: Heneb replied that “the HER does not hold information relating to this request.” This answer covered only the HER; the original question asked about wider Trust records concerning the December 1993 notification, the recommended Breach of Condition Notice, and the reference to the Disused Burial Grounds (Amendment) Act 1981, so it remains unclear whether non-HER files were searched.

items.question: Does Heneb hold the Council's reply to the 1993 breach notification or the Trust's response on Condition 18 discharge?
items.answer: Heneb replied that “the HER does not hold information relating to this request.” The reply was scoped to the HER only; the question as asked concerned the local planning authority's reply and any Trust response more broadly, so whether wider Trust records were searched is unconfirmed.

items.question: Does Heneb hold correspondence on compliance with Conditions 16, 17 and 18, including the Council's referenced letters?
items.answer: Heneb replied that “the HER does not hold information relating to this request.” The response was limited to the HER rather than the Trust's wider files, which is what the question had asked about, specifically correspondence bearing the Council's references AP/GLP/89/01396/OUT, TD/JSJ/92/00671/RES, TD/JM/92/00671/RES and TD/KH/92/00671/RES.

items.question: Does Heneb hold records of the 4 May 1994 meeting with the Council, Ideal Homes and Cotswold Archaeological Trust?
items.answer: Heneb replied that “the HER does not hold information relating to this request.” This answer was scoped to the HER only; the original question asked for the Trust's records of the meeting, including any agenda, minutes or agreed mitigation strategy/written scheme of investigation, so wider Trust holdings have not been confirmed as searched.

items.question: Does Heneb hold monitoring records on its concerns over the 1994 Cotswold Archaeological Trust excavation?
items.answer: Heneb replied that “the HER does not hold information relating to this request.” The response covered the HER only; the question had asked for the Trust's site visit notes, monitoring reports and correspondence about reservations concerning the conduct and quality of the 1994 excavation, so it is not confirmed whether wider Trust records were searched.

items.question: Does Heneb hold correspondence on the 21 March 1994 Home Office licence for disinterment of remains?
items.answer: Heneb replied that “the HER does not hold information relating to this request.” This was scoped to the HER only; the question asked about any Trust correspondence concerning the licence, including any variation or extension of it.

items.question: Does Heneb hold correspondence with Cadw between 1993 and 1995 about whether Great House Farm should be scheduled?
items.answer: Heneb replied that “the HER does not hold information relating to this request.” The reply covered the HER only; the question asked about the Trust's correspondence with Cadw on scheduling during 1993–1995.

items.question: Does Heneb hold records of what became of the 1990 watching brief at Great House Farm?
items.answer: Heneb replied that “the HER does not hold information relating to this request.” The response was scoped to the HER only; the question asked who carried out the watching brief, when, and where the resulting report is held.

items.question: Does Heneb hold the present location of site archives from the 1978–1980, 1990 and 1994 interventions?
items.answer: Heneb replied that “the HER does not hold information relating to this request.” The answer was scoped to the HER only; the question asked for the present location and accession details of the paper and digital site archives for all three interventions.

items.question: Does Heneb hold accession records for the medieval ironwork from the 1880 'armour' find at Great House Farm?
items.answer: Heneb replied that “the HER does not hold information relating to this request.” The response was scoped to the HER only; the question asked for the accession details held by the National Museum of Wales for the ironwork, and any Trust record of that identification. This matter is also raised in a pending complaint of 27 September (five-week target around 3 November), so it has not been re-asked separately.

items.question: Does Heneb hold records of the three possible 13th-century skeletons found in 1963 at Great House Farm?
items.answer: Heneb replied that “the HER does not hold information relating to this request.” The response covered the HER only; the question asked for any Trust record of the skeletons recorded by the Barry and Vale Archaeological Group, and of their present whereabouts.

items.question: Does Heneb hold records of the whereabouts/treatment, including reburial, of the 1994 Great House Farm remains?
items.answer: Heneb replied that “the HER does not hold information relating to this request.” The response was scoped to the HER only; the question asked for any Trust record of where the remains are now and how they were treated, including any reburial. This matter is also raised in a pending complaint of 27 September (five-week target around 3 November), so it has not been re-asked separately.
