Sion Buckler pointed out that his original request covered institutional/operational information (on military deployment, MACA, and interdepartmental correspondence) as well as his own personal data, and asked the MOD to confirm whether the non-personal elements had been formally handled under FOIA, in line with ICO guidance that mixed requests should be split between the applicable regimes, and if not, to register and process them as an FOI request.

items.question: Did the MOD's search extend beyond the storage facility and DBS systems to all records on the 1988 eviction?
items.answer: No reply has been received. Sion Buckler asked the MOD to clarify whether searches for his request had been confined to the storage facility and Defence Business Services systems described in its letter, or whether they had also covered other relevant MOD business areas and historical records, including any material on possible Armed Forces involvement in the 1988 eviction and any Military Aid to the Civil Authorities request.

items.question: Does the MOD hold any MACA request, assessment or record relating to Great House Farm or the 1988 eviction?
items.answer: No reply has been received. As part of a clarification of FOI2026/09019, Sion Buckler asked the MOD whether it held "any request, assessment or record of Military Aid to the Civil Authorities (MACA) relating to the location or relevant events," and, if none was held, to confirm whether that was the result of a search or evidence of prior destruction, transfer or disposal, including the date, reference and destination of any such disposal.

items.question: Does the MOD hold a search record, retention schedule or disposal entry for the non-Special-Forces FOI2026/09019 search?
items.answer: No reply has been received. Sion Buckler asked the MOD to identify which non-Special-Forces departments, record systems, date ranges and catalogue/file series were searched in response to the non-Special-Forces part of FOI2026/09019, and to say whether any search record, case note, retention schedule, transfer list or disposal entry existed that would explain what happened to potentially responsive records, asking that this be processed without the section 23(5) Special Forces exemption being applied automatically to the rest of the request.

items.question: Has the Ministry of Defence completed the internal review of FOI2026/09019 requested on 20 June 2026?
items.answer: No reply has been received. Sion Buckler asked the MOD to confirm that the internal review of FOI2026/09019, requested on 20 June 2026 and acknowledged on 4 July 2026, was still active and to provide a completion date, noting it was "outstanding, well beyond the 40 working days the MOD itself indicated" and asking that the matter be passed to the Information Rights Compliance Team. No response to this point has been recorded.

items.question: Can the Ministry of Justice comment on or intervene in the individual case concerning Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr)?
items.answer: No. The Ministry of Justice's Central Correspondence Team replied that ministers and officials cannot comment on or intervene in an individual case. The letter noted that complaints about solicitors should be directed to the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA), and signposted Citizens Advice and Law Centres for further help. The team apologised for the delay in responding.

items.question: What search terms, repositories and functions did the NPCC consult in responding to FOI 3065/2026?
items.answer: The NPCC disclosed its search methodology, listing two search terms, five repositories/source descriptions, and four consulted functions used to respond to the request.

items.question: Does the NPCC hold information responsive to questions 4 to 6 of FOI 3065/2026?
items.answer: No. The NPCC said that information relating to Q4–Q6 'is not held'. It also supplied, as a goodwill gesture, the policing-lead retrieval email, and noted that search results had already been captured by email in earlier disclosures.

items.question: Did the NPCC uphold its substantive response to FOI 3156/2026 on internal review?
items.answer: Yes. The NPCC's internal review upheld the substantive response given under FOI 3156/2026, confirming this as a separate review matter from the 2 September correspondence decision.

items.question: Does the NPCC hold any custody, transfer, retention or disposal information relevant to the request?
items.answer: The NPCC replied that it does not hold this information. It said that searches of accessible NPCC functions, shared drives, the Counter Terrorism Coordination Committee holdings and ACPO archive listings 'found no information within scope', and that no custody, transfer, retention or disposal information is held.

items.question: Does the National Library of Wales hold Bute Estate series records D153 and D205 relating to Cardiff Castle furniture?
items.answer: The National Library of Wales's internal review outcome, issued 29 July 2026, described the searches it had carried out, including the Bute Estate series D153 and D205. A further email dated 30 September 2026 asked the family to refer to this previous correspondence for details of the searches carried out, rather than providing new information. No attachment containing the full text of the internal review has been located in the family's mailbox; the library's emails of 28 and 29 July 2026 are plain text only (around 11 KB each).

items.question: Does the National Library of Wales hold records relating to Great House Farm, Llandough, Cardiff?
items.answer: The National Library of Wales responded on 29 July 2026 to FOI/2026/11, which concerned Great House Farm, Llandough, Cardiff, and the follow-on internal review outcome was issued separately under FOI/2026/09. The substantive content of the FOI/2026/11 response itself is not available: a document previously logged as "FOI2026-11-Response.pdf" could not be found in any email.

items.question: Does RCAHMW hold any record of correspondence between C.N. Johns and Mrs Buckler regarding Great House Farm?
items.answer: No extant record exists apart from a brief note. RCAHMW stated: “No record of the C.N. Johns / Mrs Buckler correspondence or allusion to the same is extant in our records, with the exception of the brief note in Archive 6048945.”

items.question: Does archive 6048945 record the date, purpose, or materials from the December 1988 site visit to Great House Farm?
items.answer: No. RCAHMW said archive 6048945 is one page, front and back, and there is no surviving record giving the date or purpose of the visit beyond the description currently catalogued, nor any associated site note, field sheet, photograph, sketch or correspondence.

items.question: Do RCAHMW's internal records for the Great House Farm accession numbers hold anything beyond what Coflein publishes?
items.answer: No. RCAHMW said its searches of internal records relating to these accession numbers revealed no further information beyond the public catalogue, and confirmed again that it holds nothing beyond the material already visible on Coflein.

items.question: Do archive records 6364275 and 6364276 relate to Great House Farm, Llandough?
items.answer: No. RCAHMW said these records had been thoroughly and physically reviewed and relate to the sites stated in the catalogue, which it identified as Tŷ Mawr, Tresimwn, and 33 Whitecross Street, Monmouth; they do not relate or allude to Great House Farm, Llandough, in any way.

items.question: Does RCAHMW hold aerial photographs that show Great House Farm, Llandough, in detail?
items.answer: RCAHMW said any aerial photographs covering the site would likely be high-altitude verticals unlikely to show the site in detail, and that it holds no further photographic record of the site in its collection.

items.question: What are the archive reference numbers for the 1974 investigator's notes and the 1988 ink plan of Great House Farm?
items.answer: RCAHMW said the 1974 investigator's notes by H.J. Thomas are archive 6048943, and the ink plan with additions made on 12/12/1988 is archive 6048941; it holds nothing beyond the material already visible on Coflein for these items.

items.question: Does RCAHMW hold any record of transfers, retention or disposal decisions for the Great House Farm archive material?
items.answer: No. RCAHMW stated: “There is no record of this.”

items.question: Does RCAHMW hold provenance information for the nineteenth-century armour deposit account from Great House Farm?
items.answer: No. RCAHMW stated: “We hold no such provenance information.”

items.question: Has RCAHMW confirmed its searches for Great House Farm records are complete and that nothing is being withheld?
items.answer: Yes. RCAHMW said its searches covered registered files, the NMRW archive by subject term and by area, and a manual search of uncatalogued material; it said nothing is withheld and that the remaining requests are answered under section 21 of FOIA because the information is accessible by other means (via Coflein). It considers the requests of 8, 15, 17 and 20 September 2026 fully answered.

items.question: Does RCAHMW hold any letters or records about Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth?
items.answer: No – RCAHMW's registered files, which it says are the only campaign records it keeps long term, contain no letters or records about the site, and nothing further has come to light since its earlier replies of 28 May, 10 June and 11 June 2026. RCAHMW stated: “there are no letters or records about this site, Tŷ Mawr Farm, Llandough, in our registered files, the only campaign records we keep long-term. No records have come to light since.” The only information it holds about the site, including its demolition, is in its archive, the National Monuments Record of Wales, accessible via Coflein (NPRN 20182); aerial-photograph searches would be chargeable.

items.question: Does the unpublished Suggett report on Great House Farm mention the late-19th-century armour find?
items.answer: RCAHMW replied that the armour find is not mentioned in Richard Suggett's unpublished report, archive 6048945, most of which is reproduced as Heneb site description GGAT02038s. It said two other records do mention the find: archive 6048942 and a Daily Telegraph article of 16 April 1974 (archive 6048944).

items.question: What material was received by RCAHMW under accession numbers NA/GL/88/49 and NA/GL/89/208 for Great House Farm?
items.answer: RCAHMW said NA/GL/88/49 is the accession entry for archive 6048945, and the only item received under NA/GL/89/208 was archive 6048941, which is reproduced in the GGAT 1990 assessment (archive 6524751).

items.question: Does Post Office Limited hold records of Mr Williams and his part in Marconi's 1897 experiments at Lavernock Point?
items.answer: No. Post Office Limited replied under reference FOI2026/00751 that it does not hold any information about Mr Williams of the Cardiff Post Office Engineering Department or his involvement in Marconi's 1897 experiments at Lavernock Point.

items.question: Does South Wales Police hold deployment or duty logs showing officer attendance at Great House Farm in late 1988?
items.answer: A response is pending. South Wales Police acknowledged FOI request 1264/26 and confirmed, in a follow-up email, 'A response will be provided to yourself within 20 working days, the deadline for which is 09/11/2026,' but has not yet supplied a substantive answer on whether deployment, duty or operational logs for the period exist.

items.question: Does South Wales Police hold liaison or police-assistance records on the 1988 Great House Farm eviction?
items.answer: A response is pending. South Wales Police acknowledged FOI request 1264/26 and stated a response would be provided by the statutory deadline of 09/11/2026, but has not yet answered whether it holds any recorded liaison or request for assistance connected with the possession, eviction, demolition, public order policing or complaint-handling at Great House Farm in 1988.

items.question: If 1988 Great House Farm operational records aren't held, do transfer/disposal entries exist, and where sent?
items.answer: A response is pending. South Wales Police has only acknowledged FOI request 1264/26 and confirmed a statutory deadline of 09/11/2026; it has not yet confirmed whether records-transfer, retention or disposal entries exist for the relevant 1988 operational record series, or identified any receiving repository if records were transferred.

items.question: Does South Wales Police hold information relating to the named individuals connected to the Great House Farm case?
items.answer: South Wales Police replied that it does not hold the information requested about the named individuals.

items.question: Does South Wales Police hold incident, sudden-death or Coroner referral records for Mary Doreen Williams's 1983 death?
items.answer: A full response has been issued but the text of the determination is not available in this correspondence. South Wales Police first acknowledged the request (ref 1040/26) and apologised for delay, saying 'We are currently dealing with a high volume of requests. Unfortunately, there are delays in the handling of some requests as a result.' It later sent a substantive reply attaching its decision, stating 'Your request for information has now been considered and our response is attached. I trust that this information answers your request,' and setting out the right to request an internal review. The content of the attached response — i.e. whether any incident reports, sudden-death reports, Coroner referrals or statements were located — is not recorded in the correspondence provided.

items.question: Will South Wales Police place a litigation hold on records relating to planning application 89/01396/OUT?
items.answer: No substantive reply has been received; only an automatic acknowledgement was sent confirming receipt of the preservation notice. South Wales Police has not yet confirmed whether a hold has been applied, named an officer responsible, or stated what, if anything, it holds in scope of the request concerning conditions 16–18 of application 89/01396/OUT, the archaeological consultation route, or the 1989 application-receipt record.

items.question: Will South Wales Police record a crime report over suspected fraud in creating title WA231076/WA240304?
items.answer: No reply has been received to this request. The requester asked South Wales Police to record, or explain in writing why it would not record, a report of suspected fraud and concealment in the creation and use of title to Great House Farm, including first registration of titles WA231076 (applied for 30 November 1982) and WA240304 (applied for 23 February 1983), and the 1987 court proceedings.

items.question: What systems, years and record series did South Wales Police search before finding no records under FOI 719/26?
items.answer: No reply has been received. The requester asked for a search note setting out the systems searched, the years covered, and whether South Wales Constabulary's 1988 paper records had been transferred to Glamorgan Archives, to support the 'no records held' response given under FOI 719/26.

items.question: Were 1988 South Wales Police records of the Great House Farm eviction destroyed, and does disposal proof survive?
items.answer: No substantive reply has been received; only an automatic acknowledgement was sent for the internal review (ref 1188/26) of FOI 719/26, which does not address the question. A further holding message confirmed the review had been passed to FOI officers to assess validity, but no answer on retention schedules or disposal records has been given.

items.question: Were any 1988 South Wales Constabulary records of the eviction transferred to Glamorgan Archives or the Heritage Centre?
items.answer: No substantive reply has been received. The internal review request of 719/26 asked South Wales Police to confirm whether records were transferred to Glamorgan Archives or the South Wales Police Heritage Centre, with the reference if known. Only an automatic acknowledgement and a holding message saying the review had been passed to FOI officers have been sent; no answer on transfer or location of records has been provided.

items.question: Will South Wales Police reconsider its 'no records held' response to FOI 719/26 given the Llandough 1988 video evidence?
items.answer: No reply has been received. On 2 August 2026 the requester asked South Wales Police to either confirm that a further search had been conducted and provide any additional records found, or explain the basis for maintaining the "no records" response given contemporaneous video evidence (including ITV material) showing police presence at Llandough in 1988, and requested a response within 5 working days. No substantive reply to this follow-up appears in the record, only an automated acknowledgement.

items.question: Does South Wales Police hold records of police or bailiff involvement in the 1988 eviction at Great House Farm?
items.answer: South Wales Police held no such records. Its substantive response to FOI request 719/26, issued on 16 July 2026 with the formal response attached, found no records were held; this is confirmed by the requester's later e-mail stating "On 16 July 2026 you issued a response to my FOI request 719/26 stating that no records were held."

items.question: Does South Wales Police hold records of complaints or use of force relating to the 1988 eviction at Great House Farm?
items.answer: South Wales Police held no such records. This question formed part of FOI request 719/26, which the force answered on 16 July 2026 by stating that no records were held, as confirmed by the requester's follow-up e-mail referring to that "no records were held" response.

items.question: Does South Wales Police hold records of military or defence personnel involvement in the 1988 Great House Farm eviction?
items.answer: South Wales Police held no such records. This was part of the same FOI request 719/26, answered on 16 July 2026 with a "no records were held" response, as confirmed by the requester's subsequent e-mail.

items.question: Did South Wales Police accept the 29 May 2026 EIR/FOIA disclosure notice about Great House Farm sent to its 101 inbox?
items.answer: South Wales Police did not process it as a request. Its automated reply stated that "South Wales Police no longer accepts reports via email" and directed the sender to call 999 in an emergency, use the Single Online Home web reporting form, or call 101 for non-emergencies. The substantive questions in the notice — about documents citing the William/Buckler family line, whether family members were recorded as owners, tenants or reporters of the 1880 find under the dining room floor, records of gaps or missing archive volumes for 1950–1989, and the reasons Cadw did not schedule the site before demolition — were not addressed.

items.question: Did the Police and Crime Commissioner's office forward this correspondence to South Wales Police?
items.answer: No. The Commissioner's office replied that it is not practice for the office to forward reporting e-mails directly to South Wales Police, noting that "The Commissioner and her team do not have access to Police systems, and it is not practice for our office to forward reporting e-mails directly to South Wales Police." The sender was advised to report operational policing matters directly to South Wales Police by dialling 101, using the force's website, or via Crimestoppers.

items.question: When were YHL/PO/JO/10/11/2536 records transferred to TNA, and what is the accession/transfer reference?
items.answer: No reply has been received to this part of the internal review request, which asked The National Archives to confirm the date the physical records in YHL/PO/JO/10/11/2536 were transferred into its custody and to supply the accession/transfer reference.

items.question: Does the transfer paperwork for YHL/PO/JO/10/11/2536 name the transferring body, held by TNA by August 2026?
items.answer: No reply has been received. The internal review asked whether the transfer paperwork identifies the body that transferred the records and whether the physical records were already in The National Archives' custody at the time of the earlier August 2026 enquiries.

items.question: Does the 20 May 2026 date for YHL/PO/JO/10/11 refer only to the publication of catalogue metadata on Discovery?
items.answer: No reply has been received to this question, which asked The National Archives to clarify whether 20 May 2026 marks solely the publication date of catalogue metadata rather than any transfer or release of the physical records.

items.question: Why was BP Properties Ltd excluded from The National Archives' initial search, and is there a search log or audit trail?
items.answer: No reply has been received. The internal review asked why BP Properties Ltd, named in the original request, was excluded from the initial search of the four property/location terms within the PRO and RW series, and whether a search log or audit trail exists for that search.

items.question: Were any searches run between 20 May 2026 and 13 August 2026 that included 'BP Properties Ltd' or the case title?
items.answer: No reply has been received to this question about whether any searches were conducted between 20 May 2026 and 13 August 2026 that included the terms 'BP Properties Ltd' or the case title.

items.question: Do BP Properties v Buckler transfer records show prior custody, direct transfer, or material withheld/destroyed?
items.answer: No reply has been received. The internal review asked whether the transfer records show the date of transfer, previous custody, whether the material came directly from the Parliamentary Archives, and whether any associated material was excluded, withheld, destroyed or retained elsewhere, and requested that any 'not held' answer distinguish between records never transferred, transferred elsewhere, destroyed/disposed of, or simply lacking a discoverable catalogue reference.

items.question: What search terms did The National Archives use when looking for records relating to Great House Farm?
items.answer: The National Archives said its initial search used only four terms within two series, and this was later widened. It stated: "The initial response from our records enquiries team looked for the four terms (“Great House Farm”, “Ty Mawr”, “Llandough” or “Cedfin”) within the PRO and RW series and did not find any relevant information. We have now tried those terms and the further twelve terms that you have specified in a wider catalogue search."

items.question: Does The National Archives hold any records relating to Western Ground Rents Ltd in connection with Great House Farm?
items.answer: No. The National Archives' expanded search found nothing: "Western Ground Rents Ltd — Relevant information not found."

items.question: Does The National Archives hold any records relating to BP Pension Trust Ltd in connection with Great House Farm?
items.answer: No. The National Archives stated: "BP Pension Trust Ltd — Relevant information not found."

items.question: Does The National Archives hold any records relating to Mountjoy Ltd in connection with Great House Farm?
items.answer: No. The National Archives stated: "Mountjoy Ltd — Relevant information not found."

items.question: Does The National Archives hold any 1982–1983 registration or administrative records relating to Great House Farm?
items.answer: No. The National Archives stated: "1982–1983 registration and associated government or administrative records — Relevant information not found."

items.question: Does TNA hold records of 1980-1988 public campaign activity and government correspondence on Great House Farm?
items.answer: No. The National Archives stated: "1980–1988 public campaign and governmental correspondence — Relevant information not found."

items.question: Does The National Archives hold National Farm Survey records covering Great House Farm in the 1940s?
items.answer: Possibly, but this has not been confirmed by search. The National Archives said: "There are likely to be records of the farm in the 1940s as part of the National Farm Survey series but these cannot all currently be searched online by farm," and that it would need to charge a fee to carry out that research.

items.question: Does TNA hold Glamorgan Agricultural Executive Committee minutes or papers mentioning Great House Farm?
items.answer: The National Archives holds Glamorgan Agricultural Executive Committee minutes and papers generally, but could not confirm whether any mention Great House Farm without a paid search. It said: "There are Agricultural Executive Committee minutes and papers for Glamorgan; but again, these cannot be searched online by name of farm and we are unable to conduct this research without charging a fee."

items.question: What is the catalogue reference and Discovery release date for the BP Properties v Buckler HL judicial papers?
items.answer: The National Archives disclosed that the papers are held as container HL/PO/JO/10/11/2536 (barcode P104629), item 19 'BP Properties Ltd v Buckler', within series YHL/PO/JO/10/11, which was released onto its Discovery catalogue on 20 May 2026. The disclosure included the release schedule, a high-level delivery schedule, and a Collection 27 Series 11 manifest as supporting CSV files.

items.question: Does the Manorial Documents Register hold a manor return for Llandough relevant to Great House Farm?
items.answer: The National Archives' Manorial Documents Register forwarded a return for the manor of Llandough, reference HMC 9.311. It cautioned that which 'Llandough' the return actually concerns should be checked against the document itself, given that similarly-named places/records can cause confusion.

items.question: Will the Council's Scrutiny Committee undertake a Task and Finish Review into Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr)?
items.answer: No, the Council declined to take this forward. Democratic and Scrutiny Services replied that it would be "unable to consider" the suggestion, explaining that Task and Finish work is reserved for "strategic" county-wide policy topics rather than review of "individual historical decisions", that planning matters "should be navigated through other channels", and that because the issue was already being raised with "Welsh Government, CADW, MSs and MPs" it would "not be appropriate" for Scrutiny to add a further layer of stakeholders.

items.question: Can the Council identify the three missing appendices to the Great House Farm planning file by their original reference?
items.answer: No reply has been received to this chase request. The Council was asked on 10 October 2026 to identify the three missing appendices by reference or description and to confirm the response date for FOI/EIR 00211557, said to remain on or about 26 October 2026, but no reply is recorded.

items.question: Will the Council disclose the three missing Great House Farm planning appendices or state the exemption relied on?
items.answer: No reply has been received. This was asked as part of a 10 October 2026 chase of FOI/EIR 00211557, with a response then due on or about 26 October 2026.

items.question: Does the statutory response date for FOI/EIR 00211557 remain on or about 26 October 2026?
items.answer: No reply confirming or denying this has been received. The question was put in a 10 October 2026 chase email; no response is recorded.

items.question: Does the Vale of Glamorgan Registration Service hold a death record for Mary (Nancy) Williams?
items.answer: No death record for Mary (Nancy) Williams could be found in the Vale of Glamorgan registers. The Superintendent Registrar "could not find a death record" locally and passed the enquiry on to the Cardiff registration service; the outcome of that onward enquiry is not yet in the record.

items.question: Has the Council described what further documentation was located in its September 2026 sift for EIR request 00210772?
items.answer: No reply has been received to this point. In a formal chase dated 7 October 2026, Mr Buckler asked the Council to provide 'a non-disclosive description of the further documentation located (date range, creator/supplier, how it came into the Council's possession, approximate volume)'. He noted that 'you have not identified a single document found in the September sift' and that the Council had not named any third-party consultee class, the date any consultation was sent, or the date a reply was required. No response addressing this point is in the corpus.

items.question: Has the Council confirmed that documentation found in its further search for EIR 00210772 is being preserved unaltered?
items.answer: No reply has been received. The 7 October 2026 chase specifically asked for 'confirmation that the newly located documentation is being preserved without alteration, destruction or disposal', and separately asked the Council to 'confirm in writing that every document in the sift, and every related planning, enforcement, legal, committee, land, finance and correspondence record ... is under a formal preservation hold and will not be destroyed'. No confirmation of a preservation hold appears in the corpus.

items.question: Will the Council release disclosable material from its further search without awaiting third-party consultation?
items.answer: No reply has been received. The 7 October 2026 chase requested 'immediate release of any material that can properly be disclosed without awaiting third-party consultation' in respect of EIR 00210772. The Council had not, by that date, named any third-party consultee class, the date consultation was sent, or the date a reply was required, and no partial release is recorded in the corpus.

items.question: What did the Council's planning register show for 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES, and what's missing from disclosure?
items.answer: No substantive answer has been given yet. The Council's reply of 30 September 2026 was only an acknowledgement of receipt of FOI/EIR 00211557, stating the request was "being considered under the terms of the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and the Environmental Information Regulations 2004" and that a full response would follow "within 20 working days" (due on or about 26 October 2026). It did not address the planning-register question.

items.question: Does the Council hold Appendix B (the further GGAT comments) to the officer's report on 89/01396/OUT?
items.answer: No substantive answer has been given yet. The 30 September 2026 reply to FOI/EIR 00211557 was an acknowledgement only, confirming the request was being considered and that a response was due within 20 working days (on or about 26 October 2026); it did not address Appendix B specifically, including whether it still exists, when it may have left the file, or under what retention rule.

items.question: Does the Council hold its October 1990 confirmation that condition 17 on 89/01396/OUT had been complied with?
items.answer: No substantive answer has been given yet. The Council's 30 September 2026 reply to FOI/EIR 00211557 was an acknowledgement of receipt only, with a response due within 20 working days (on or about 26 October 2026).

items.question: Does the Council hold the 1993-94 papers on whether condition 18 was discharged, including GGAT's December 1993 letters?
items.answer: No substantive answer has been given yet. The Council's 30 September 2026 reply to FOI/EIR 00211557 was an acknowledgement of receipt only, with a response due within 20 working days (on or about 26 October 2026).

items.question: Did the Council make and record an environmental-assessment screening determination for 89/01396/OUT?
items.answer: No substantive answer has been given yet. The Council's 30 September 2026 reply to FOI/EIR 00211557 was an acknowledgement of receipt only, with a response due within 20 working days (on or about 26 October 2026).

items.question: What statutory consultation route applied to 89/01396/OUT given the site's SMR status?
items.answer: No substantive answer has been given yet. The Council's 30 September 2026 reply to FOI/EIR 00211557 was an acknowledgement of receipt only, with a response due within 20 working days (on or about 26 October 2026).

items.question: Does the Council hold the September 1992 reserved-matters approval for 92/00671/RES, with an archaeological condition?
items.answer: No substantive answer has been given yet. The Council's 30 September 2026 reply to FOI/EIR 00211557 was an acknowledgement of receipt only, with a response due within 20 working days (on or about 26 October 2026).

items.question: Who removed the commemorative tree planted at Great House Farm, and under what authority?
items.answer: The Council has not yet confirmed whether it holds records on this; the enquiry has been passed to its Information Governance Team to check. Replying on behalf of the Leader on 18 September 2026 to an escalation about ward member silence, the Monitoring Officer stated: “In relation to the tree, I am making enquiries to establish whether the Council holds any records which may assist in answering your question regarding its removal. This is being dealt with by the Information Governance Team, I have copied in the FOI unit email domain. If relevant information is held by the Council, I will advise you accordingly. Equally, if no such records are held, I will confirm that position.” The matter has therefore been redirected into the formal FOI/EIR process (see separate request ref 00211484) rather than answered directly.

items.question: Does the Council hold the complete County Engineer consultation response referenced in the report for 89/01396/OUT?
items.answer: A substantive answer remains pending. The Council acknowledged this request on 18 September 2026 under reference 00211483, stating it would respond 'within 20 working days unless the Council does not hold the information or there is a reason for it to be withheld.' No further, substantive response has been received.

items.question: Does the Council hold records of when NRA and County Engineer responses on 89/01396/OUT were received and filed?
items.answer: A substantive answer remains pending. The Council acknowledged this request on 18 September 2026 under reference 00211483, stating it would respond 'within 20 working days unless the Council does not hold the information or there is a reason for it to be withheld.' No further, substantive response has been received.

items.question: Does the Council hold records on how the 1990 evaluation informed application 92/00671/RES?
items.answer: A substantive answer remains pending. The Council acknowledged this request on 18 September 2026 under reference 00211483, stating it would respond 'within 20 working days unless the Council does not hold the information or there is a reason for it to be withheld.' No further, substantive response has been received.

items.question: Does the Council hold a document explaining the change from 18 to 20 dwellings at Great House Farm?
items.answer: A substantive answer remains pending. The Council acknowledged this request on 18 September 2026 under reference 00211483, stating it would respond 'within 20 working days unless the Council does not hold the information or there is a reason for it to be withheld.' No further, substantive response has been received.

items.question: Does the Council hold correspondence on the retention, preservation or demolition of Great House Farm farmhouse?
items.answer: A substantive answer remains pending. The Council acknowledged the request on 17 September 2026 under reference 00211463, stating it would respond 'within 20 working days unless the Council does not hold the information or there is a reason for it to be withheld.' items.question: When did the Williams family come to Great House, and on what terms?
items.answer:
The 1667 date rests on Mary (Nancy) Williams's c. 1974 statement and the 1974 press reports that repeat it. No document of 1667 has been found. The family's own correspondence describes 1667 three ways: a purchase, continuous occupation 'since at least 1667', and a lease for 999 years. The heritage record (Suggett 1988, GGAT02038s) says the Vaughans, a minor gentry family, occupied Great House as the chief freehold farm from the mid-16th to the late 18th century. Both can be true only if the Williamses held under the Vaughans (as tenants or lessees) before the Bute purchase.

Points for:
• Mary (Nancy) Williams's statement (c. 1974)
• 1974 newspaper reports
• Family tradition of nine generations
• Western Mail, 20 November 1958 (snippet only): Mrs M. D. Buckler tells the county planning committee the land was "farmed by her family since 1667"

Points against:
• RCAHMW Archive 6048945 / Heneb GGAT02038s: Vaughans occupied the house mid-C16 to late C18
• No 1667 deed, lease, court roll entry or fine located in any archive searched

Records still to check:
• 1670 Glamorgan hearth tax (published, Welsh Journals Online): who was the householder at Great House?
• TNA E 179/221/297 and E 179/221/294
• Glamorgan land tax 1691–1707 (DBJ/O/90-94)
• NLW Bute deeds: any lease of Great House c.1660–75 or for 999 years; the Vaughan-to-Bute conveyance and its recitals
• Earls of Pembroke papers (WSHC 2057)

items.question: When and how did the Bute Estate acquire Great House from the Vaughans?
items.answer:
Bute bought the lordship of the manor in 1793. The heritage record says Bute acquired the freehold of Great House in the early 19th century. The conveyance from the Vaughans or their heirs has not been located, so the date, the price and any leases it recited are unknown.

Points for:
• Heneb GGAT02038s / RCAHMW Archive 6048945: 'In the early C19 the freehold was acquired by the Bute Estate'

Records still to check:
• NLW Bute Estate Records: the Vaughan conveyance and abstract of title
• Mount Stuart: Bute estate deeds (research visit)

items.question: In 1877, did Bute sell the farmhouse and about 10 acres to Daniel Thomas, or only lease quarrying rights?
items.answer:
Mary's statement says Bute sold the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres to Daniel Thomas in 1877 and kept about 9 acres, with the house to pass to the Williamses when quarrying ended. No deed has been found. Glamorgan Archives found no deeds for an 1877 Daniel Thomas transaction (2026/4097b) and pointed to Bute X.6(12), the Bute trustees' 1877 abstract of payments and receipts at Cardiff Library. DBDT/79/1, a May 1877 lease to a John Williams, was examined and is a Pembroke Terrace, Cardiff property, not Llandough (2026/3893). A capital receipt from Daniel Thomas in Bute X.6(12) would point to a sale; a rent or royalty would point to a lease.

Points for:
• Mary (Nancy) Williams's statement (c. 1974)
• Western Ground Rents and BP later dealt with the farmhouse and garden as a separate unit (1959, 1962, 1965, 1975, 1983)

Points against:
• No 1877 deed located at Glamorgan Archives (2026/4097b)
• NLW FOI/2026/09 searches of Bute series D153 and D205 did not produce it

Records still to check:
• Bute X.6(12) at Cardiff Library / Cathays Heritage Library (enquiry sent 10 Oct 2026; FOI draft ready)
• NLW D153/1–8 (Llandough deeds) — enquiry 27 Sep and 10 Oct 2026
• Mount Stuart: Bute accounts 1875–1880

items.question: Is the 1881 census's "Llandough Home Farm" Great House Farm?
items.answer:
Very probably, on who lived there; not on the name. The census household (RG11/5288 p.2, schedule 9) is John Williams, 53, farmer, born at Leckwith. Directories of 1868, 1875 and 1880, and of 1887, 1891 and 1901, list "Williams John, Great house" / "Great House farm, Llandough", and list the Rees family separately at Llandough Farm. The South Wales Star of 1892 has "Mr. John Williams, Great House Farm, Llandough". Per Sion Buckler, the census entered Great House Farm under the wrong name. No other source uses "Home Farm".

Points for:
• 1881 census RG11/5288 p.2 (EV-0224): John Williams household
• Slater's 1868, Worrall's 1875, Slater's 1880: "Williams John, Great house" (EV-0225)
• Owen's 1887 and 1891, Cardiff Directory 1901: "Williams John, Great House farm, Llandough" (EV-0225)
• South Wales Star, 10 June 1892: "Mr. John Williams, Great House Farm, Llandough" (EV-0226)
• Llandough Farm held by the Rees family, 1861–1910 (Cardiff Times 1865; Weekly Mail 1886; Evening Express 1898, 1910) (EV-0228)

Points against:
• "Home Farm" appears in no other source found: newspapers 1804–1919, directories or OS maps
• The acreage reads 170 or 120: 170 fits Llandough Farm (166 acres, 1824–32) better than Great House (about 120 acres, 1841 tithe)
• The press sometimes calls a Williams "of Llandough Farm" (1895, 1903, 1904), so the farm names were confused in print too
• EV-0223 carries a different, dictated reading of the name, not shown on this page

Records still to check:
• Folio and enumeration district for RG11/5288 p.2
• The 1871 and 1891 census entries for the same household
• Bute rentals and surveys for the farm under any name, 1855–1908

items.question: Was the farm's water cut off, when, by whom, and why?
items.answer:
Mrs M. D. Buckler (Mary (Nancy) Williams) told Glamorgan County Council's planning committee in November 1958 that "the water was cut off from her house and grounds for nearly 10 years by order of Western Ground Rents" (Western Mail, 20 November 1958, snippet only). Per Branwen Buckler (voice testimony), the council cut it over bills that Mary (Nancy) Williams insisted were paid, cattle drowned in the River Ely trying to reach water, and it was raised in Parliament. In the 1950s Llandough was in Penarth Urban District; Cardiff Corporation was the public water undertaker for the area, and in 1914 the Bute estate also supplied part of Penarth Urban District from a private spring at Llandough.

Points for:
• Western Mail, 20 November 1958, p.7 (snippet only): "by order of Western Ground Rents" (EV-0037)
• Branwen Buckler (voice testimony, 19 October 2026)
• Water undertakings return, 1914: a Bute estate spring supplying part of Penarth Urban District

Points against:
• The 1958 report names the landlord, not a council or a water bill
• No report of cattle drowning in the Ely found
• No Commons or Lords debate or written answer found, 1946–92 (committees and MPs' letters not searched)
• Dŵr Cymru's 2026 replies refer to a disconnection in the 1980s: possibly a second cut-off

Records still to check:
• The full Western Mail page, 20 November 1958, and the South Wales Echo and Penarth Times for that week
• Glamorgan County Council planning committee minutes, 19 November 1958
• Penarth UDC and Cardiff Corporation waterworks committee minutes, 1948–58
• Whether the farm was on the mains or an estate spring or pipe

items.question: Who was involved in the eviction and demolition of 30 November – 6 December 1988?
items.answer:
Press reports record the eviction on 30 November and demolition from about 4am on 6 December 1988 by BP Properties. South Wales Police reported no records under FOI 719/26 (internal review 1188/26); on FOI 1264/26 (operational records) the force asked on 13 Oct 2026 for the names of individuals or entities involved, and suspended the clock under s.10(6) until clarified. The MOD relied on section 23(5) for the Special Forces element of FOI2026/09019.

• Press archive (Western Mail, South Wales Echo, December 1988)

• MOD internal review DPR2026/46503
• RCAHMW: Suggett's post-demolition visit, Archive 6048945

items.question: Was the house ever fully recorded, and what happened to the C. N. Johns / Mrs Buckler correspondence?
items.answer:
RCAHMW's record (Suggett, Archive 6048945) says the ground floor was surveyed in 1974 by H. J. Thomas, the house 'remained partially recorded because of problems of access created by an ownership dispute', and it was demolished before it could be examined. The same record says correspondence between C. N. Johns and Mrs Buckler 'has been lost from the file since 1986/87'. RCAHMW reports no further trace of that correspondence or of the purpose of Suggett's visit (RC26-0375, 29 Sep and 6 Oct 2026).

• RC26-0375 replies

items.question: Was a soldier in armour found under the dining-room floor, and where are the finds?
items.answer:
Two RCAHMW records repeat the account (Archive 6048942; Daily Telegraph, 16 April 1974, Archive 6048944, 'in about 1870'). Museum Wales reports no record of acquiring such finds (FOI 2026-024 and internal review). The source of the 'held by the National Museum of Wales' attribution has not been traced.

• Source pending (no named witness)

Points against:

items.question: How did the woodland (WA735527) leave the family's possession?
items.answer:
The woodland is registered to the Forest of Cardiff (WA735527), which offered the family a route to ownership in September 2026; the family declined. Per the Buckler case, the woodland of Parcel A was taken in 1955 and passed through a couple in Llandough (SOURCE PENDING). No price is recorded for the charity's 1994 acquisition.

items.question: What happened to Mary's 1974 ownership claim?
items.answer:
In the 1974 county court action Mary pleaded ownership and the Limitation Act 1939. The case was part heard, adjourned and not relisted. In 1987 the court relied on the 1974 letters as making her occupation permissive; her ownership plea was never decided.
